target_customer: Enterprises and security integrators with CCTV estates (offices, retail, transport) buying video analytics via API, on premises or edge appliances
problem: Finding and counting people across many camera streams normally relies on facial recognition, which is restricted or banned in some places; operators also drown in false alarms.
business_model: Usage and license based AI video analytics API with on premises and hybrid deployments

founders.name: Kostyantyn Shysh
previous_startups: Unmorph (founder, per YC page; outcome not found)
founders.background_notes: Prior employers and education not found in sources opened. Source: YC company page, TechCrunch 2019-08-15.

technical_complexity.rationale: Person re-identification across cameras without faces needs custom deep learning models and attribute detection at video scale; TechCrunch noted the approach did not scale well to large manhunts.

defensibility.rationale: Differentiation was a non-face approach, but re-identification research was public and larger video platforms could add similar search; no data or integration lock-in was shown.

incumbents: Established video management and surveillance vendors
takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copy was reported in sources found; the company remains active and by 2025 markets generative AI alarm processing.

market_need_then: In 2019 several US cities had restricted facial recognition and TechCrunch tied the pitch to that backlash, with founders targeting the US and UK for their dense CCTV coverage.

branding.domain_note: Uses traces.ai; acquisition history not found.

brand_strength.rationale: Brand coverage was limited to launch press (TechCrunch, Ukrainian outlets, a podcast) and a B2B site; no community or brand-specific press found.

outcome_analysis: Traces launched at the Summer 2019 batch with a privacy friendly alternative to facial recognition and has stayed active for years with about ten staff. No priced round beyond YC was found in verifiable sources, so its traction is unclear; its site now stresses generative AI alarm handling and forensic search, which suggests a move up from basic person tracking.
notes: Aggregators disagree on funding: SeedTable lists a $150K seed in 2019-08, Dealroom $125K, CB Insights $150K total and a 2024-09 Google for Startups Ukraine Support Fund round; all single aggregator figures and unverified, not recorded as rounds. Interfax and Kyiv Post items on a Ukrainian startup raising 200000 euros could not be tied to Traces (interfax fetch was rate limited). Competitors: a dated search found no 2019 sources naming rivals, so the list is empty. Outcome search found no acquisition, shutdown or layoffs.
